13.15187fbe98:
<n>133:1</n> Ecce nunc benedícite Dóminum, * omnes servi Dómini:
<n>133:1</n> Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
<n>133:2</n> In nóctibus extóllite manus vestras in sancta, * et benedícite Dóminum.
<n>133:3</n> Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
13.a9bcecf161:
<n>133:1</n> Behold now bless ye the Lord, * all ye servants of the Lord:
<n>133:1</n> Who stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.
<n>133:2</n> In the nights lift up your hands to the holy places, * and bless ye the Lord.
<n>133:3</n> May the Lord out of Sion bless thee, * he that made heaven and earth.
13.f4afeb6589:
<n>137:1</n> Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * quóniam audísti verba oris mei.
<n>137:1</n> In conspéctu Angelórum psallam tibi: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo.
<n>137:2</n> Super misericórdia tua, et veritáte tua: * quóniam magnificásti super omne, nomen sanctum tuum.
<n>137:3</n> In quacúmque die invocávero te, exáudi me: * multiplicábis in ánima mea virtútem.
<n>137:4</n> Confiteántur tibi, Dómine, omnes reges terræ: * quia audiérunt ómnia verba oris tui:
<n>137:5</n> Et cantent in viis Dómini: * quóniam magna est glória Dómini.
<n>137:6</n> Quóniam excélsus Dóminus, et humília réspicit: * et alta a longe cognóscit.
<n>137:7</n> Si ambulávero in médio tribulatiónis, vivificábis me: * et super iram inimicórum meórum extendísti manum tuam, et salvum me fecit déxtera tua.
<n>137:8</n> Dóminus retríbuet pro me: * Dómine, misericórdia tua in sǽculum: ópera mánuum tuárum ne despícias.
13.870bbc741a:
<n>137:1</n> I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: * for thou hast heard the words of my mouth.
<n>137:1</n> I will sing praise to thee in the sight of the Angels: * I will worship towards thy holy temple, and I will give glory to thy name.
<n>137:2</n> For thy mercy, and for thy truth: * for thou hast magnified thy holy name.
<n>137:3</n> In what day soever I shall call upon thee, hear me: * thou shalt multiply strength in my soul.
<n>137:4</n> May all the kings of the earth give glory to thee: * for they have heard all the words of thy mouth.
<n>137:5</n> And let them sing in the ways of the Lord: * for great is the glory of the Lord.
<n>137:6</n> For the Lord is high, and looketh on the low: * and the high he knoweth afar off.
<n>137:7</n> If I shall walk in the midst of tribulation, thou wilt quicken me: * and thou hast stretched forth thy hand against the wrath of my enemies: and thy right hand hath saved me.
<n>137:8</n> The Lord will repay for me: * thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: O despise not the works of thy hands.
13.1be898406b:
<n>134:1</n> Laudáte nomen Dómini, * laudáte, servi, Dóminum.
<n>134:2</n> Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
<n>134:3</n> Laudáte Dóminum, quia bonus Dóminus: * psállite nómini eius, quóniam suáve.
<n>134:4</n> Quóniam Iacob elégit sibi Dóminus, * Israël in possessiónem sibi.
<n>134:5</n> Quia ego cognóvi quod magnus est Dóminus, * et Deus noster præ ómnibus diis.
<n>134:6</n> Ómnia quæcúmque vóluit, Dóminus fecit in cælo, et in terra, * in mari, et in ómnibus abýssis.
<n>134:7</n> Edúcens nubes ab extrémo terræ: * fúlgura in plúviam fecit.
<n>134:7</n> Qui prodúcit ventos de thesáuris suis: * qui percússit primogénita Ægýpti ab hómine usque ad pecus.
<n>134:9</n> Et misit signa, et prodígia in médio tui, Ægýpte: * in Pharaónem, et in omnes servos eius.
<n>134:10</n> Qui percússit gentes multas: * et occídit reges fortes:
<n>134:11</n> Sehon, regem Amorrhæórum, et Og, regem Basan, * et ómnia regna Chánaan.
<n>134:12</n> Et dedit terram eórum hereditátem, * hereditátem Israël, pópulo suo.
<n>134:13</n> Dómine, nomen tuum in ætérnum: * Dómine, memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.
<n>134:14</n> Quia iudicábit Dóminus pópulum suum: * et in servis suis deprecábitur.
<n>134:15</n> Simulácra géntium argéntum, et aurum, * ópera mánuum hóminum.
<n>134:16</n> Os habent, et non loquéntur: * óculos habent, et non vidébunt.
<n>134:17</n> Aures habent, et non áudient: * neque enim est spíritus in ore ipsórum.
<n>134:18</n> Símiles illis fiant qui fáciunt ea: * et omnes qui confídunt in eis.
<n>134:19</n> Domus Israël, benedícite Dómino: * domus Aaron, benedícite Dómino.
<n>134:20</n> Domus Levi, benedícite Dómino: * qui timétis Dóminum, benedícite Dómino.
<n>134:21</n> Benedíctus Dóminus ex Sion, * qui hábitat in Ierúsalem.
13.5acfcbb48c:
<n>134:1</n> Praise ye the name of the Lord: * O you his servants, praise the Lord:
<n>134:2</n> You that stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.
<n>134:3</n> Praise ye the Lord, for the Lord is good: * sing ye to his name, for it is sweet.
<n>134:4</n> For the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself: * Israel for his own possession.
<n>134:5</n> For I have known that the Lord is great, * and our God is above all gods.
<n>134:6</n> Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done, in heaven, in earth, * in the sea, and in all the deeps.
<n>134:7</n> He bringeth up clouds from the end of the earth: * he hath made lightnings for the rain.
<n>134:7</n> He bringeth forth winds out of his stores: * He slew the firstborn of Egypt from man even unto beast.
<n>134:9</n> He sent forth signs and wonders in the midst of thee, O Egypt: * upon Pharao, and upon all his servants.
<n>134:10</n> He smote many nations, * and slew mighty kings:
<n>134:11</n> Sehon king of the Amorrhites, and Og king of Basan, * and all the kingdoms of Chanaan.
<n>134:12</n> And gave their land for an inheritance, * for an inheritance to his people Israel.
<n>134:13</n> Thy name, O Lord, is for ever: * thy memorial, O Lord, unto all generations.
<n>134:14</n> For the Lord will judge his people, * and will be entreated in favour of his servants.
<n>134:15</n> The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, * the works of men’s hands.
<n>134:16</n> They have a mouth, but they speak not: * they have eyes, but they see not.
<n>134:17</n> They have ears, but they hear not: * neither is there any breath in their mouths.
<n>134:18</n> Let them that make them be like to them: * and every one that trusteth in them.
<n>134:19</n> Bless the Lord, O house of Israel: * bless the Lord, O house of Aaron.
<n>134:20</n> Bless the Lord, O house of Levi: * you that fear the Lord, bless the Lord.
<n>134:21</n> Blessed be the Lord out of Sion, * who dwelleth in Jerusalem.
13.6956d0a132:
<n>130:1</n> Dómine, non est exaltátum cor meum: * neque eláti sunt óculi mei.
<n>130:1</n> Neque ambulávi in magnis: * neque in mirabílibus super me.
<n>130:2</n> Si non humíliter sentiébam: * sed exaltávi ánimam meam:
<n>130:2</n> Sicut ablactátus est super matre sua, * ita retribútio in ánima mea.
<n>130:3</n> Speret Israël in Dómino, * ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
13.31e1f66291:
<n>130:1</n> O Lord, my heart is not exalted: * nor are my eyes lofty.
<n>130:1</n> Neither have I walked in great matters, * nor in wonderful things above me.
<n>130:2</n> If I was not humbly minded, * but exalted my soul:
<n>130:2</n> As a child that is weaned is towards his mother, * so reward in my soul.
<n>130:3</n> Let Israel hope in the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.
13.ff68fc1379:
<n>131:1</n> Meménto, Dómine, David, * et omnis mansuetúdinis eius:
<n>131:2</n> Sicut iurávit Dómino, * votum vovit Deo Iacob:
<n>131:3</n> Si introíero in tabernáculum domus meæ, * si ascéndero in lectum strati mei:
<n>131:4</n> Si dédero somnum óculis meis, * et pálpebris meis dormitatiónem:
<n>131:5</n> Et réquiem tempóribus meis: donec invéniam locum Dómino, * tabernáculum Deo Iacob.
<n>131:6</n> Ecce, audívimus eam in Éphrata: * invénimus eam in campis silvæ.
<n>131:7</n> Introíbimus in tabernáculum eius: * adorábimus in loco, ubi stetérunt pedes eius.
<n>131:8</n> Surge, Dómine, in réquiem tuam, * tu et arca sanctificatiónis tuæ.
<n>131:9</n> Sacerdótes tui induántur iustítiam: * et sancti tui exsúltent.
<n>131:10</n> Propter David, servum tuum, * non avértas fáciem Christi tui.
<n>131:11</n> Iurávit Dóminus David veritátem, et non frustrábitur eam: * De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
<n>131:12</n> Si custodíerint fílii tui testaméntum meum, * et testimónia mea hæc, quæ docébo eos:
<n>131:12</n> Et fílii eórum usque in sǽculum, * sedébunt super sedem tuam.
<n>131:13</n> Quóniam elégit Dóminus Sion: * elégit eam in habitatiónem sibi.
<n>131:14</n> Hæc réquies mea in sǽculum sǽculi: * hic habitábo quóniam elégi eam.
<n>131:15</n> Víduam eius benedícens benedícam: * páuperes eius saturábo pánibus.
<n>131:16</n> Sacerdótes eius índuam salutári: * et sancti eius exsultatióne exsultábunt.
<n>131:17</n> Illuc prodúcam cornu David, * parávi lucérnam Christo meo.
<n>131:18</n> Inimícos eius índuam confusióne: * super ipsum autem efflorébit sanctificátio mea.
13.19f162f406:
<n>131:1</n> Lord, remember David, * and all his meekness.
<n>131:2</n> How he swore to the Lord, * he vowed a vow to the God of Jacob:
<n>131:3</n> If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house: * if I shall go up into the bed wherein I lie:
<n>131:4</n> If I shall give sleep to my eyes, * or slumber to my eyelids,
<n>131:5</n> Or rest to my temples: until I find out a place for the Lord, * a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.
<n>131:6</n> Behold we have heard of it in Ephrata: * we have found it in the fields of the wood.
<n>131:7</n> We will go into his tabernacle: * we will adore in the place where his feet stood.
<n>131:8</n> Arise, O Lord, into thy resting place: * thou and the ark, which thou hast sanctified.
<n>131:9</n> Let thy priests be clothed with justice: * and let thy saints rejoice.
<n>131:10</n> For thy servant David’s sake, * turn not away the face of thy anointed.
<n>131:11</n> The Lord hath sworn truth to David, and he will not make it void: * of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne.
<n>131:12</n> If thy children will keep my covenant, * and these my testimonies which I shall teach them:
<n>131:12</n> Their children also for evermore * shall sit upon thy throne.
<n>131:13</n> For the Lord hath chosen Sion: * he hath chosen it for his dwelling.
<n>131:14</n> This is my rest for ever and ever: * here will I dwell, for I have chosen it.
<n>131:15</n> Blessing I will bless her widow: * I will satisfy her poor with bread.
<n>131:16</n> I will clothe her priests with salvation: * and her saints shall rejoice with exceeding great joy.
<n>131:17</n> There will I bring forth a horn to David: * I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.
<n>131:18</n> His enemies I will clothe with confusion: * but upon him shall my sanctification flourish.
13.dc849cc5ff:
<n>132:1</n> Ecce quam bonum et quam iucúndum, * habitáre fratres in unum:
<n>132:2</n> Sicut unguéntum in cápite, * quod descéndit in barbam, barbam Aaron,
<n>132:2</n> Quod descéndit in oram vestiménti eius: * sicut ros Hermon, qui descéndit in montem Sion.
<n>132:3</n> Quóniam illic mandávit Dóminus benedictiónem, * et vitam usque in sǽculum.
13.aa0935984b:
<n>132:1</n> Behold how good and how pleasant it is * for brethren to dwell together in unity:
<n>132:2</n> Like the precious ointment on the head, * that ran down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron,
<n>132:2</n> Which ran down to the skirt of his garment: * as the dew of Hermon, which descendeth upon mount Sion.
<n>132:3</n> For there the Lord hath commanded blessing, * and life for evermore.
13.b9c0e404ea:
<n>135:1</n> Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:2</n> Confitémini Deo deórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:3</n> Confitémini Dómino dominórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:4</n> Qui facit mirabília magna solus: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:5</n> Qui fecit cælos in intelléctu: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:6</n> Qui firmávit terram super aquas: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:7</n> Qui fecit luminária magna: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:8</n> Solem in potestátem diéi: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:9</n> Lunam, et stellas in potestátem noctis: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
13.74c38ab4d9:
<n>135:1</n> Praise the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:2</n> Praise ye the God of gods: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:3</n> Praise ye the Lord of lords: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:4</n> Who alone doth great wonders: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:5</n> Who made the heavens in understanding: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:6</n> Who established the earth above the waters: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:7</n> Who made the great lights: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:8</n> The sun to rule the day: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:9</n> The moon and the stars to rule the night: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
13.5183672986:
<n>135:10</n> Qui percússit Ægýptum cum primogénitis eórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:11</n> Qui edúxit Israël de médio eórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:12</n> In manu poténti, et brácchio excélso: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:13</n> Qui divísit Mare Rubrum in divisiónes: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:14</n> Et edúxit Israël per médium eius: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:15</n> Et excússit Pharaónem, et virtútem eius in Mari Rubro: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:16</n> Qui tradúxit pópulum suum per desértum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:17</n> Qui percússit reges magnos: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:18</n> Et occídit reges fortes: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:19</n> Sehon, regem Amorrhæórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:20</n> Et Og, regem Basan: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:21</n> Et dedit terram eórum hereditátem: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:22</n> Hereditátem Israël, servo suo: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:23</n> Quia in humilitáte nostra memor fuit nostri: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:24</n> Et redémit nos ab inimícis nostris: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:25</n> Qui dat escam omni carni: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:26</n> Confitémini Deo cæli: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
<n>135:26</n> Confitémini Dómino dominórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
13.5980a5c75d:
<n>135:10</n> Who smote Egypt with their firstborn: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:11</n> Who brought out Israel from among them: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:12</n> With a mighty hand and with a stretched out arm: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:13</n> Who divided the Red sea into parts: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:14</n> And brought out Israel through the midst thereof: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:15</n> And overthrew Pharao and his host in the Red sea: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:16</n> Who led his people through the desert: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:17</n> Who smote great kings: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:18</n> And slew strong kings: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:19</n> Sehon king of the Amorrhites: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:20</n> And Og king of Basan: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:21</n> And he gave their land for an inheritance: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:22</n> For an inheritance to his servant Israel: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:23</n> For he was mindful of us in our affliction: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:24</n> And he redeemed us from our enemies: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:25</n> Who giveth food to all flesh: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:26</n> Give glory to the God of heaven: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
<n>135:26</n> Give glory to the Lord of lords: * for his mercy endureth for ever.
13.723bdecb6a:
<n>136:1</n> Super flúmina Babylónis, illic sédimus et flévimus: * cum recordarémur Sion:
<n>136:2</n> In salícibus in médio eius, * suspéndimus órgana nostra.
<n>136:3</n> Quia illic interrogavérunt nos, qui captívos duxérunt nos, * verba cantiónum:
<n>136:3</n> Et qui abduxérunt nos: * Hymnum cantáte nobis de cánticis Sion.
<n>136:4</n> Quómodo cantábimus cánticum Dómini * in terra aliéna?
<n>136:5</n> Si oblítus fúero tui, Ierúsalem, * oblivióni detur déxtera mea.
<n>136:6</n> Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, * si non memínero tui:
<n>136:6</n> Si non proposúero Ierúsalem, * in princípio lætítiæ meæ.
<n>136:7</n> Memor esto, Dómine, filiórum Edom, * in die Ierúsalem:
<n>136:7</n> Qui dicunt: Exinaníte, exinaníte * usque ad fundaméntum in ea.
<n>136:8</n> Fília Babylónis mísera: * beátus, qui retríbuet tibi retributiónem tuam, quam retribuísti nobis.
<n>136:9</n> Beátus, qui tenébit, * et allídet párvulos tuos ad petram.
13.3ba1157ecf:
<n>136:1</n> Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: * when we remembered Sion:
<n>136:2</n> On the willows in the midst thereof * we hung up our instruments.
<n>136:3</n> For there they that led us into captivity required of us * the words of songs.
<n>136:3</n> And they that carried us away, said: * Sing ye to us a hymn of the songs of Sion.
<n>136:4</n> How shall we sing the song of the Lord * in a strange land?
<n>136:5</n> If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, * let my right hand be forgotten.
<n>136:6</n> Let my tongue cleave to my jaws, * if I do not remember thee:
<n>136:6</n> If I make not Jerusalem * the beginning of my joy.
<n>136:7</n> Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom, * in the day of Jerusalem:
<n>136:7</n> Who say: Rase it, rase it, * even to the foundation thereof.
<n>136:8</n> O daughter of Babylon, miserable: * blessed shall he be who shall repay thee thy payment which thou hast paid us.
<n>136:9</n> Blessed be he that shall take * and dash thy little ones against the rock.
13.643f15db92:
<n>138:1</n> Dómine, probásti me, et cognovísti me: * tu cognovísti sessiónem meam, et resurrectiónem meam.
<n>138:3</n> Intellexísti cogitatiónes meas de longe: * sémitam meam, et funículum meum investigásti.
<n>138:4</n> Et omnes vias meas prævidísti: * quia non est sermo in lingua mea.
<n>138:5</n> Ecce, Dómine, tu cognovísti ómnia novíssima, et antíqua: * tu formásti me, et posuísti super me manum tuam.
<n>138:6</n> Mirábilis facta est sciéntia tua ex me: * confortáta est, et non pótero ad eam.
<n>138:7</n> Quo ibo a spíritu tuo? * et quo a fácie tua fúgiam?
<n>138:8</n> Si ascéndero in cælum, tu illic es: * si descéndero in inférnum, ades.
<n>138:9</n> Si súmpsero pennas meas dilúculo, * et habitávero in extrémis maris:
<n>138:10</n> Étenim illuc manus tua dedúcet me: * et tenébit me déxtera tua.
<n>138:11</n> Et dixi: Fórsitan ténebræ conculcábunt me: * et nox illuminátio mea in delíciis meis.
<n>138:12</n> Quia ténebræ non obscurabúntur a te, et nox sicut dies illuminábitur: * sicut ténebræ eius, ita et lumen eius.
<n>138:13</n> Quia tu possedísti renes meos: * suscepísti me de útero matris meæ.
13.1ae4055fc4:
<n>138:1</n> Lord, thou hast proved me, and known me: * thou hast known my sitting down, and my rising up.
<n>138:3</n> Thou hast understood my thoughts afar off: * my path and my life thou hast searched out.
<n>138:4</n> And thou hast foreseen all my ways: * for there is no speech on my tongue.
<n>138:5</n> Behold, O Lord, thou hast known all things, the last and those of old: * thou hast formed me, and hast laid thy hand upon me.
<n>138:6</n> Thy knowledge is become wonderful to me: * it is high, and I cannot reach to it.
<n>138:7</n> Whither shall I go from thy spirit? * or whither shall I flee from thy face?
<n>138:8</n> If I ascend into heaven, thou art there: * if I descend into hell, thou art present.
<n>138:9</n> If I take my wings early in the morning, * and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea:
<n>138:10</n> Even there also shall thy hand lead me: * and thy right hand shall hold me.
<n>138:11</n> And I said: Perhaps darkness shall cover me: * and night shall be my light in my pleasures.
<n>138:12</n> But darkness shall not be dark to thee, and night shall be light as the day: * the darkness thereof, and the light thereof are alike to thee.
<n>138:13</n> For thou hast possessed my reins: * thou hast protected me from my mother’s womb.
13.b4a8c3d0e4:
<n>138:14</n> Confitébor tibi quia terribíliter magnificátus es: * mirabília ópera tua, et ánima mea cognóscit nimis.
<n>138:15</n> Non est occultátum os meum a te, quod fecísti in occúlto: * et substántia mea in inferióribus terræ.
<n>138:16</n> Imperféctum meum vidérunt óculi tui, et in libro tuo omnes scribéntur: * dies formabúntur, et nemo in eis.
<n>138:17</n> Mihi autem nimis honorificáti sunt amíci tui, Deus: * nimis confortátus est principátus eórum.
<n>138:18</n> Dinumerábo eos, et super arénam multiplicabúntur: * exsurréxi, et adhuc sum tecum.
<n>138:19</n> Si occíderis, Deus, peccatóres: * viri sánguinum, declináte a me:
<n>138:20</n> Quia dícitis in cogitatióne: * Accípient in vanitáte civitátes tuas.
<n>138:21</n> Nonne qui odérunt te, Dómine, óderam? * et super inimícos tuos tabescébam?
<n>138:22</n> Perfécto ódio óderam illos: * et inimíci facti sunt mihi.
<n>138:23</n> Proba me, Deus, et scito cor meum: * intérroga me, et cognósce sémitas meas.
<n>138:24</n> Et vide, si via iniquitátis in me est: * et deduc me in via ætérna.
13.a8c1cf4d8a:
<n>138:14</n> I will praise thee, for thou art fearfully magnified: * wonderful are thy works, and my soul knoweth right well.
<n>138:15</n> My bone is not hidden from thee, which thou hast made in secret: * and my substance in the lower parts of the earth.
<n>138:16</n> Thy eyes did see my imperfect being, and in thy book all shall be written: * days shall be formed, and no one in them.
<n>138:17</n> But to me thy friends, O God, are made exceedingly honourable: * their principality is exceedingly strengthened.
<n>138:18</n> I will number them, and they shall be multiplied above the sand: * I rose up and am still with thee.
<n>138:19</n> If thou wilt kill the wicked, O God: * ye men of blood, depart from me:
<n>138:20</n> Because you say in thought: * They shall receive thy cities in vain.
<n>138:21</n> Have I not hated them, O Lord, that hated thee: * and pined away because of thy enemies?
<n>138:22</n> I have hated them with a perfect hatred: * and they are become enemies to me.
<n>138:23</n> Prove me, O God, and know my heart: * examine me, and know my paths.
<n>138:24</n> And see if there be in me the way of iniquity: * and lead me in the eternal way.
13.7ca36e659f:
<n>139:2</n> Éripe me, Dómine, ab hómine malo: * a viro iníquo éripe me.
<n>139:3</n> Qui cogitavérunt iniquitátes in corde: * tota die constituébant prǽlia.
<n>139:4</n> Acuérunt linguas suas sicut serpéntis: * venénum áspidum sub lábiis eórum.
<n>139:5</n> Custódi me, Dómine, de manu peccatóris: * et ab homínibus iníquis éripe me.
<n>139:5</n> Qui cogitavérunt supplantáre gressus meos: * abscondérunt supérbi láqueum mihi:
<n>139:6</n> Et funes extendérunt in láqueum: * iuxta iter scándalum posuérunt mihi.
<n>139:7</n> Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu: * exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
<n>139:8</n> Dómine, Dómine, virtus salútis meæ: * obumbrásti super caput meum in die belli.
<n>139:9</n> Ne tradas me, Dómine, a desidério meo peccatóri: * cogitavérunt contra me, ne derelínquas me, ne forte exalténtur.
<n>139:10</n> Caput circúitus eórum: * labor labiórum ipsórum opériet eos.
<n>139:11</n> Cadent super eos carbónes, in ignem deícies eos: * in misériis non subsístent.
<n>139:12</n> Vir linguósus non dirigétur in terra: * virum iniústum mala cápient in intéritu.
<n>139:13</n> Cognóvi quia fáciet Dóminus iudícium ínopis: * et vindíctam páuperum.
<n>139:14</n> Verúmtamen iusti confitebúntur nómini tuo: * et habitábunt recti cum vultu tuo.
13.84bc366b42:
<n>139:2</n> Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: * rescue me from the unjust man.
<n>139:3</n> Who have devised iniquities in their hearts: * all the day long they designed battles.
<n>139:4</n> They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent: * the venom of asps is under their lips.
<n>139:5</n> Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the wicked: * and from unjust men deliver me.
<n>139:5</n> Who have proposed to supplant my steps: * the proud have hidden a net for me.
<n>139:6</n> And they have stretched out cords for a snare: * they have laid for me a stumbling block by the wayside.
<n>139:7</n> I said to the Lord: Thou art my God: * hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication.
<n>139:8</n> O Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation: * thou hast overshadowed my head in the day of battle.
<n>139:9</n> Give me not up, O Lord, from my desire to the wicked: * they have plotted against me; do not thou forsake me, lest they should triumph.
<n>139:10</n> The head of them compassing me about: * the labour of their lips shall overwhelm them.
<n>139:11</n> Burning coals shall fall upon them; thou wilt cast them down into the fire: * in miseries they shall not be able to stand.
<n>139:12</n> A man full of tongue shall not be established in the earth: * evil shall catch the unjust man unto destruction.
<n>139:13</n> I know that the Lord will do justice to the needy, * and will revenge the poor.
<n>139:14</n> But as for the just, they shall give glory to thy name: * and the upright shall dwell with thy countenance.

<n>138:3</n> Intellexísti cogitatiónes meas de longe: * sémitam meam, et funículum meum investigásti.
<n>138:4</n> Et omnes vias meas prævidísti: * quia non est sermo in lingua mea.
<n>138:5</n> Ecce, Dómine, tu cognovísti ómnia novíssima, et antíqua: * tu formásti me, et posuísti super me manum tuam.
<n>138:6</n> Mirábilis facta est sciéntia tua ex me: * confortáta est, et non pótero ad eam.
<n>138:7</n> Quo ibo a spíritu tuo? * et quo a fácie tua fúgiam?
<n>138:8</n> Si ascéndero in cælum, tu illic es: * si descéndero in inférnum, ades.
<n>138:9</n> Si súmpsero pennas meas dilúculo, * et habitávero in extrémis maris:
<n>138:10</n> Étenim illuc manus tua dedúcet me: * et tenébit me déxtera tua.
<n>138:11</n> Et dixi: Fórsitan ténebræ conculcábunt me: * et nox illuminátio mea in delíciis meis.
<n>138:12</n> Quia ténebræ non obscurabúntur a te, et nox sicut dies illuminábitur: * sicut ténebræ eius, ita et lumen eius.
<n>138:13</n> Quia tu possedísti renes meos: * suscepísti me de útero matris meæ.

<n>138:3</n> Thou hast understood my thoughts afar off: * my path and my life thou hast searched out.
<n>138:4</n> And thou hast foreseen all my ways: * for there is no speech on my tongue.
<n>138:5</n> Behold, O Lord, thou hast known all things, the last and those of old: * thou hast formed me, and hast laid thy hand upon me.
<n>138:6</n> Thy knowledge is become wonderful to me: * it is high, and I cannot reach to it.
